naslov: What worked (and didn't) in 12 NBA season debuts: LeBron, LaMelo, more stars
tekst:
Newly minted Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant said it best Wednesday: "You only get one chance at a first impression."
Though the Blazers were one of several teams to ace their season openers, there were also plenty of stars who might want a do-over. After all, Jayson Tatum's Boston Celtics blew a 22-point lead to the Pistons, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama shot 1-for-13 in a loss to the rival Oklahoma City Thunder, and Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami Heat were blown off their home court by the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Let's run through the NBA's opening-week action -- through Thursday, every team will have played at least once -- with an eye toward the first impressions made by key players suiting up for new teams this season. Which ones launched with ease, and which succumbed to false starts?
Jump to a season debut
Great: Kawhi | Dame | Kessler | OKC starting 5
Good: LaMelo | LeBron | AD | PG-13 | Garland
Rough: Giannis | Yaxel vs. Luka | Miles Bridges
Great first impressions
Kawhi Leonard, Raptors
The schedule-makers gifted Leonard a home opener against the lowly Chicago Bulls on Wednesday, and the two-time Finals MVP took full advantage. Leonard wasted no time moving past a tumultuous summer marked by a delayed trade and the NBA's lengthy salary cap circumvention investigation, enjoying a hearty welcome back from the Toronto crowd before scoring 23 points and snagging four steals in a blowout victory.
The scariest part for East rivals: Leonard didn't have his signature midrange jumper dialed in and played only 24 minutes, yet the Raptors still managed a 43-point margin of victory that tied for the fifth largest in franchise history.
Toronto ran up the score with excellent balance across its starting lineup, as Leonard, Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley each surpassed 20 points. How high can Leonard lift an offense that ranked 15th last season?
Damian Lillard, Trail Blazers
The Blazers' icon spent Wednesday putting his career back on track after a forgettable two-year detour with the Bucks and an Achilles injury that sidelined him last season. In his first game for Portland since 2023, the nine-time All-Star guard provided such an emotional jolt that the Blazers stormed out to a preposterous 21-0 lead and cruised to a 124-83 blowout of the Phoenix Suns.
No one will argue with the results from the opener, but it remains an open question whether Lillard and Morant are the ideal starting backcourt for Portland. Against Phoenix, Lillard scored 25 points and hit six 3-pointers, and Morant added 14 points and eight assists in only 23 minutes.
Tougher tests await: The Suns lack big and physical perimeter playmakers capable of exploiting Portland's undersized guards. But it's nice to see Lillard back where he belongs in Rip City.
Walker Kessler, Lakers
Well, it's hard to beat perfect. Kessler made all 12 of his shots, including 10 dunks, and grabbed nine rebounds in the Lakers' blowout of the Warriors on Wednesday. Not bad for a guy playing in his first regular-season game since last October and in his first game for the Lakers since arriving from the Jazz in a summer sign-and-trade deal.
After only one game, Kessler already looks like the best center Luka Doncic has played with in his nine-year career. "Inside the NBA'''s Shaquille O'Neal went even further, opining that Kessler is "the best big man in the NBA."
Slow down, Shaq: The Lakers' smashing debut came against an injury-plagued Warriors team that rolled over after halftime.
Still, Kessler earned praise from Lakers coach JJ Redick for his ability to change ends quickly. The 7-foot-2 center clearly understands that his gigantic frame won't do him any good if he's stuck trailing the action. If Kessler can put together a complete season from a health standpoint and continue to serve as a constant vertical target, then Doncic will be a major factor in the MVP discussion.
Thunder starters
Technically, Oklahoma City's most important newcomer has been Aday Mara, a 7-foot-3 rookie center who made quite the splash in his NBA debut by swatting Wembanyama at the rim. But the Thunder also trotted out a tweaked starting lineup after trading longtime starter Luguentz Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in a cost-cutting move this summer.
Cason Wallace stepped into Dort's sport, filling out an imposing group that includes two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, All-Stars Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren and center Isaiah Hartenstein. In a convincing road win over San Antonio on Tuesday, the Thunder starters exhibited excellent discipline and togetherness while frustrating Wembanyama from start to finish. Two days later, Oklahoma City overcame poor outside shooting to put away another top West challenger: Nikola Jokic's Denver Nuggets.
Oklahoma City also got key boosts from Mara, guard Jared McCain and veteran stopper Alex Caruso this week. With Williams healthy, it's not too early to ask whether Oklahoma City's rotation is actually better than the 2025 championship team and last season's group that led the league with 64 wins.
Good first impressions
LaMelo Ball, Timberwolves
Ball did his part to position the Timberwolves as lightning rods by shuffling a good 10 feet without incurring a traveling violation while launching a step-back 3-pointer against the Heat. Clips of his comical sidestepping immediately went viral, prompting the NBA referees' association to clarify on social media that an infraction had occurred: "[Ball] takes four steps after gathering the ball and travels."
Detractors will paint Ball's looseness as evidence that the modern NBA game has slipped into a less serious endeavor, while proponents will point out that Ball's new partnership with Anthony Edwards is wildly fun. Both sides make valid points, but the loud and brash Timberwolves can't be dismissed as frivolous after absolutely wrecking the new-look Heat in Miami.
